split.rule: On a day with attack windows, windows before the first-to-last attack span are train, the span is 60/15/25 with purge gaps, and windows after the span are test. A day with no attack windows stays 60/15/25.
split.f1_definition: macro-F1 over proxy stages with test support, excluding classes marked n too small
split.persistence: repeats the logistic_window predicted current stage; oracle_persistence_unattainable repeats the true current stage
split.host_rule: The same network-level attack-span time boundaries are applied to every host. A missing host-window inside a sequence is a zero vector with active 0.

notes.name: excluded_attacks
notes.text: DoS, DDoS and Web Attacks are excluded.

notes.name: missing_stages
notes.text: Reconnaissance and exfiltration have no real data.

notes.name: coverage
notes.text: BruteForce appears on one capture day and Bot on one.

notes.name: granularity
notes.text: Each row is one source host in one 60-second window. The host address is not a feature.

notes.name: logistic
notes.text: Both logistic models are class-weighted L2 logistic regression. On the full-data run the single-window model is fit with lbfgs and the flattened 10-window model is fit with averaged SGD on the same loss for at most 40 epochs, because an exact fit took about 55 minutes per horizon on 528,521 sequences and the process exited before that sweep finished. SGD reached the iteration cap before its tolerance on most horizons. One full-data fit is reused across seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, so the logistic standard deviation is zero. The seeds change the LSTM. The budgeted runs fit their own logistic models and do not reuse this fit.

notes.name: procedure_full
notes.text: Main metrics, onset, per-stage scores, network alarm, and the block bootstrap use the full-data procedure on seeds 0, 1, 2, 3. Seeds 0-3 were already saved (v3_host_lstm_seed0..3.pt and the matching logistic joblib files) and were reused without retraining. Seed 4 was not trained. The wall-clock gaps between the saved full-data LSTM artifacts v3_host_lstm_seed0.pt through v3_host_lstm_seed3.pt are 79.4 min, 23.5 min, 54.3 min, and the fastest is 23.5 minutes, which is not under 20 minutes. Full-data rows are not averaged with budgeted rows.

notes.name: procedure_budget
notes.text: Ablation, leave-one-attack-out, and cross_day use only the budgeted procedure, with seeds 0, 1. That procedure keeps the full test split and fits on a stratified sample of at most 25000 training anchors and 8000 validation anchors. The LSTM runs for at most 4 epochs with patience 2. The flattened logistic uses averaged SGD for at most 12 iterations. These rows are not averaged with the full-data results.

notes.name: mean_std_verdict
notes.text: LSTM beats both logistic variants and persistence by more than one standard deviation on macro-F1 at no horizon. It does not at h0 (logistic_window lstm 0.6034±0.0188 vs 0.7315±0.0000, persistence lstm 0.6034±0.0188 vs 0.7315±0.0000); h1 (persistence lstm 0.5748±0.0139 vs 0.7215±0.0000); h3 (persistence lstm 0.5761±0.0159 vs 0.7131±0.0000); h5 (persistence lstm 0.5768±0.0233 vs 0.7047±0.0000).

notes.name: verdict
notes.text: 95% block bootstrap: LSTM macro-F1 does not exceed both logistic variants and persistence at any horizon. Blocks are 30 consecutive windows, 200 resamples. It does not at h0 (logistic_window (0/4 seeds, mean CI -0.1746±0.0137 to -0.0976±0.0204); persistence (0/4 seeds, mean CI -0.1746±0.0137 to -0.0976±0.0204)); h1 (persistence (0/4 seeds, mean CI -0.1853±0.0168 to -0.0978±0.0121)); h3 (persistence (0/4 seeds, mean CI -0.1815±0.0152 to 0.1335±0.0167)); h5 (persistence (0/4 seeds, mean CI -0.1702±0.0217 to 0.1345±0.0261)).

notes.name: representation
notes.text: The host representation is better. Both the LSTM and the flattened logistic have a higher mean macro-F1 than the network-level models.
